text:
alex: FYI customer ACME opened a ticket — p99 latency jumped ~4x over the last 3 hours on /generate. CS says timeouts and retries increasing.
kevin: on it, I can already see a big jump in prefix-cache miss rate for the runtime pool serving acct-us-east.
maya: confirming. Metrics -> kv_eviction_count and prefix_miss_rate both spike around 10:12 UTC when p95/p99 climb. attaching quick log excerpt below.
alex: logs: ```[2026-03-17T10:12:03Z] kv_eviction_count=4523 prefix=acct:usr:* miss_rate=0.87 p95=420ms p99=1.2s pool=runtime-4```
jin: customer repro (from CS): repeated parallel requests with varying X-Template-ID and X-User-Tag headers. curl script shows latency reproduce locally for us.
kevin: initial hypothesis: high-cardinality client headers + per-request template ids are being folded into cache keys -> key fingerprint explosion -> continuous evictions -> cold prefix thrash.
maya: that fits the pattern: eviction-driven warmup loops. Also saw header-key cardinality spike on the ingress: ```histogram header_X-User-Tag: top 10000 unique values```
kevin: quick mitigation options (I can run these right now):
  - enable prefix-key canonicalization for the ACME route (strip nonessential headers)
  - temporarily increase KV cache size for pool runtime-4
  - set short sticky TTL for new prefixes (e.g., 5m) to reduce churn
jin: for CS: we'll ask ACME to stop sending per-request randomness while we patch. I'll open a support escalation note. :+1:
maya: command to bump cache size (nonblocking change):
```bash
# scale max keys for runtime pool (prod)
kubectl set env deploy/runtime KV_CACHE_MAX_KEYS=200000 -n prod
```
kevin: also deploying a canary with LFU-style eviction for this pool to see difference. If LFU reduces churn, we consider global rollout.
alex: ticket link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-12345 — assigning root-cause hypothesis: cache key entropy from client-supplied headers leading to eviction spiral.
maya: short-term rollback plan: if p99 doesn't fall within 10m after changes, fallback to route-level model downgrade (smaller model) and engage rate-limiter for ACME to protect overall SLA.
deploy-bot: deploy started runtime/patch-eviction-fix @7001112250 — canary to 10% of runtime-4 pool.
kevin: monitoring dashboards updated (added eviction_count, prefix_hotset_cardinality, miss_rate). Watching alert: evict_rate > 100/min.
jin: CS notified ACME with repro steps + expected mitigation window (15–30m).
alex: followups: kevin (triage + canary monitoring), maya (metrics dashboard + auto-alert tuning), jin (customer comms). I'll draft postmortem after stabilization.
kevin: confirmed metrics trending down 12m after config changes; p99 from 1.2s -> 320ms on canary. Will keep observing.
alex: thanks team. We'll push longer-term fixes: canonicalized cache keys (strip headers), LFU eviction option, and auto-warm top-n prefixes on scale-up.
